ITQAN:v2p373/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p373/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p373/r1.claim: سميا is glossed as offspring; an anonymous poetic line is cited in support.
ITQAN:v2p373/r1.anchor: قال أخبرني عن قوله تعالى ﴿ هل تعلم له سميا ﴾ قال ولدا أما سمعت قول الشاعر

STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r13.claim: The surah moves from revelation by God’s command to criticism of the Prophet and Quran, rejects claims God has a child, and ends with the silence of destroyed generations.
STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r13.anchor: After a reminder in v. 64 that revelation only comes to the Prophet by God’s Command, the sūrah proceeds to address the criticisms leveled against the Prophet and the Quranic message

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Gabriel’s speech urges the Prophet to wait steadfastly for God’s decree and not hurry.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Through the tongue of Gabriel, the Prophet (sws) is directed to be patient and wait for the decree of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Gabriel’s words urge patience and clarify that he and the angels have no independent agency: they only follow God’s commands.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: God’s directives. There is a special background to this advice and explanation given by him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Because revelation is the Prophet’s support in conflict, he naturally awaits Gabriel anxiously; like a soldier awaiting guidance, he must wait for help at its appointed time, as Qur’anic instruction elsewhere also teaches.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the sole support for the Prophet (sws) against his opponents in this phase of conflict with his opponents was divine revelation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The final question may be Gabriel’s speech or a divine insertion, but the meaning is unchanged; Islahi prefers that Gabriel is speaking because the Prophet is watched over by the Lord of all creation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: My own inclination is towards the first probability. It is Gabriel who urged the Prophet (sws) to wait and exercise patience

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Worship here has its wider sense of obedience, as it does in 19:44.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: here worhsip is used in its wider connotation and also includes obedience

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The emphatic form of the word for perseverance magnifies the meaning; with the preposition lām, it also conveys waiting, nuances difficult to preserve in translation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: It has a greater amount of stress in it. It should be kept in mind that increase in letters of a word magnifies its meaning too.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Because God has no peer, no one can thwart his intentions; the Prophet should continue his work and God will ease his hardships and accomplish his purposes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: when there is no peer or match of God, who can hinder His intentions to materialize

BURSEVI:v5p267/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p267/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p267/r1.claim: An omitted He is predicates the phrase: God owns the heavens, earth, and their creatures, so forgetfulness cannot be ascribed to Him.
BURSEVI:v5p267/r1.anchor: من الخلق فكيف يجوز النسيان على الرب

BURSEVI:v5p267/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p267/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p267/r2.claim: Worship means carrying out what one is commanded and undertaking obedience to commands and prohibitions.
BURSEVI:v5p267/r2.anchor: والعبادة قيام العبد بما تعبد به وتكلف من امتثال الأوامر والنواهي

BURSEVI:v5p267/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p267/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p267/r3.claim: Inward worship involves body following the Law, self opposing its desires, heart turning from world to afterlife, secret detaching from both realms for God, and spirit surrendering existence for witnessing.

BURSEVI:v5p267/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p267/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p267/r4.claim: Persist through worship's hardships; do not grieve over delayed revelation, mockery, or enemies' delight, because God watches over and cares for you.
BURSEVI:v5p267/r4.anchor: اصبر لمشاقها ولا تحزن بإبطاء الوحي واستهزاء الكفرة

BURSEVI:v5p267/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p267/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p267/r5.claim: The lām implies standing firm for worship through trials, unlike the ʿalā in the command about family prayer.
BURSEVI:v5p267/r5.anchor: وتعدية الاصطبار باللام لا بحرف الاستعلاء كما في قوله {واصطبر عليها}

BURSEVI:v5p267/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p267/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p267/r6.claim: Samiy means namesake, partner, equal, or likeness; the verse denies anyone worthy of God's name or any being called God alongside Him.
BURSEVI:v5p267/r6.anchor: السمي الشريك في الاسم والمثل والشبيه أي : مثلا يستحق أن يسمى إلها

BURSEVI:v5p267/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p267/r7.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p267/r7.claim: Al-Kashifi says even idolaters never called their objects Allah; divine majesty protected this supreme name while believers invoke it in ease and hardship.
BURSEVI:v5p267/r7.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (يكى از آثار سطوت آلهي آن بودكه هي كس ازاهل شرك

BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r1.claim: A Persian couplet calls the divine name a wondrous charm of the heart and a complete remembrance of the soul.
BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r1.anchor: الله الله ه طرفه نامست اين حرزدل وردجان تمامست اين

BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r2.claim: An anecdote says a ruler who called himself Allah died when his insides burned; Pharaoh called himself the highest lord but could not claim to be Allah.
BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r2.anchor: روي أن بعض الجبابرة سمى نفسه بلفظ الجلالة فصهر ما في بطنه

BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says no one may be named al-Rahman except God.
BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما لا يسمى أحد الرحمن وغيره

BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r4.speaker: المولى الفناري
BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r4.claim: Al-Fanari says Allah is exclusive in designation and use, Rahman in use, and Rahim is not exclusive; calling Musaylima Rahman was deliberate unbelief.
BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r4.anchor: قال المولى الفناري في ترتيب أسماء البسملة : إن لاسم الجلالة اختصاصا وضعيا

BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r5.claim: Quraysh accused a Yamama teacher called Rahman of teaching Muhammad; the answer identifies God as his Lord and teacher, and divine names such as Rahman or Creator should not be assigned to people.
BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r5.anchor: قالت قريش لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بلغنا أنك إنما يعلمك رجل باليمامة

BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p267#2/r6.claim: The Prophet changed the name al-Aziz because a servant's proper condition is humility and submission.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r4.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r4.claim: The angel's obedience in movement and stillness prepares the command to worship and persevere, and makes the juxtaposition with the ignorant, unjust human an elegant aside.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p113/r4.anchor: ولهذا صرح بعده بقوله تعالى ( فاعبده واصطبر لاعبادته )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r1.claim: Calling God Lord of the heavens and earth explains why forgetfulness is impossible: the owner of all cannot neglect His chosen messenger; رب is either a predicate of an omitted subject or apposition to ربك.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r1.anchor: بيان لاستحالة النسيان عليه تعالى من بيده ملكوت السموات والأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r2.claim: The imperative فاعبده follows from God's complete lordship, or from His not abandoning the Prophet or forgetting people's deeds; knowing His lordship entails worship and endurance.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r2.anchor: لترتيب ما بعدها من موجب الأمرين على ما قبلها من كونه تعالى رب السموات والأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r3.claim: The command also reassures the Prophet not to grieve over delayed revelation or unbelievers' words, since God watches over and cares for him.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r3.anchor: ولا تحزن بابطاء الوحي وكلام الكفرة فانه سبحانه يراقبك ويراعيك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء، الأخفش
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows رب السماوات to be a subject and فاعبده its predicate, with an extra فاء according to al-Akhfash; the author calls this implausible.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r4.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء أن يكون ( رب السموات ) مبتدأ والخبر ( فاعبده ) والفاء زائده

ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows وما كان ربك نسيا to continue the pious people's speech only if رب is a predicate of an omitted subject, not if it is apposition.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r5.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري أن يكون قوله تعالى : ( وما كان ربك نسيا ) من تتمة كلام المتقين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r6.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r6.claim: Al-Kashf argues that making the command a response to an omitted condition about knowing Paradise's state weakens the eloquence by leaving the obvious cause.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r6.anchor: لا يلائم كما في الكشف فصاحة التنزيل للعدول عن السبب الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r7.claim: اصطبر is paired with ل rather than the usual على because it conveys standing firm through hardships encountered in worship, like a fighter holding against an opponent.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r7.anchor: لتضمنه معنى الثبات للعبادة فيما تورد عليه من الشدائد والمشاق

ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r8.claim: This wording signals the struggle of worship and steadfastness, with an allusion to the saying about returning from the lesser jihad to the greater jihad.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p115/r8.anchor: وشمة من معنى رجعنا من الجهاد الأصغر إلى الجهاد الأكبر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p116/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p116/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، ابن جبير، قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p116/r1.claim: They explain سمي as an equal or match; because sharing a name implies likeness, it can mean a counterpart. Ibn Atiyya similarly glosses it as one equal or parallel.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p116/r1.anchor: أي مثلا كما جاء في رواية جماعة عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وابن جبير وقتادة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p116/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p116/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p116/r2.claim: Other interpretations specify a partner in the name Lord of the heavens and earth, in the divine name Allah, in Allah or al-Rahman, or in the name God in its true sense rather than a false attribution.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p116/r2.anchor: أن يراد ههنا الشريك في اسم خاص قد عبر عنه تعالى بذلك وهو رب السموات والأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v16p116/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p116/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p116/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, when asked by Nafi ibn al-Azraq, interprets سمي as a child; the same view is reported from al-Dahhak and supported with a poetic line.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p116/r3.anchor: وأخرج الطستى عن ابن عباس أن نافع ابن الازرق سأله عن ذلك فقال : السمي الولد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p116/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p116/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p116/r4.claim: Whatever interpretation is adopted, denying knowledge of a match emphatically denies that any match exists; the question establishes the duty to worship God.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p116/r4.anchor: فالمراد بانكار العلم ونفيه إنكار المعلوم ونفيه على أبلغ وجه واكده والجملة تقرير

ALUSI-FULL:v16p116/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p116/r5.speaker: الكسائي، هشام، علي بن نصر، هارون عن أبي عمرو، الحسن، الأعمش، عيسى، ابن محيصن
ALUSI-FULL:v16p116/r5.claim: They assimilate the ل into ت in هتعلم; Abu Ubayda says this is a dialect alongside clear pronunciation, and a line by Muzahim al-Uqayli witnesses the form هتعين.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p116/r5.anchor: وقرأ الأخوان وهشام وعلي بن نصر وهرون كلاهما عن أبى عمرو والحسن والأعمش

ALUSI-FULL:v16p145#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145#2/r10.claim: One gloss of God's having no namesake is that none is a counterpart worth turning to or asking for anything.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145#2/r10.anchor: مثلا يلتفت اليه ويطلب منه شئ

ALUSI-FULL:v16p145#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145#2/r11.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145#2/r11.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl asks whether anyone truly deserves, in reality, to be called by one of God's names.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145#2/r11.anchor: وقال الحسين بن الفضل : هل يستحق أحد أن يسمى باسم من اسمائه تعالى على الحقيقة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244#2/r1.claim: Worship God and persevere in worship by patiently observing His commands and prohibitions.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244#2/r1.anchor: فاعبده واصطبر لعبادته} أي: اصبر على أمره ونهيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets “namesake” as an equal or counterpart to God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244#2/r2.anchor: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: مثلا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244#2/r3.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244#2/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi asks whether anyone besides God is called Allah.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p244#2/r3.anchor: الكلبي: هل تعلم أحدا يسمى "الله" غيره

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:65/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:65/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:65/r1.claim: “Lord of the heavens” explains why God cannot forget; it is a predicate of an omitted subject or appositive. The Prophet should worship and persevere through hardship, delayed revelation, and mockery.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:65/r1.anchor: بيان لامتناع النسيان عليه، وهو خبر محذوف

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:65/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:65/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:65/r2.claim: Namesake means a peer deserving divinity or anyone named Allah; idolaters call idols gods but never Allah. Since none resembles God or deserves worship, one must submit and serve Him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:65/r2.anchor: مثلا يستحق أن يسمى إلها أو أحدا سمي الله

QASHANI:19:64-65/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:64-65/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:64-65/r5.claim: God nurtures each heaven, earth, and intervening realm by its fitting name and manages and bestows according to its state, encompassing all through His names.
QASHANI:19:64-65/r5.anchor: { رب السموات والأرض وما بينهما } يرب كلا منهما باسم يخصه ويدبره ويفيض ما يقتضيه حاله عليه فيرب الكل بجميع أسمائه

QASHANI:19:64-65/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:64-65/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:64-65/r6.claim: Worship according to one's state creates readiness for effusion and revelation; purification must be continuous rather than done once or twice.
QASHANI:19:64-65/r6.anchor: { فاعبده } بعبادتك التي يقتضيها حالك حتى تستعد لقبول الفيض ونزول الوحي ولا يكفي وجود العبادة بتهيئة الاستعداد بالتصفية مرة أو مرتين

QASHANI:19:64-65/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:64-65/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:64-65/r7.claim: Patience in worship means continuously directing oneself to God.
QASHANI:19:64-65/r7.anchor: { واصطبر } لعبادته بالتوجه إليه على الدوام

QASHANI:19:64-65/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:64-65/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:64-65/r8.claim: Having no namesake means no equal toward whom one should turn instead of God to receive one's desired gift.
QASHANI:19:64-65/r8.anchor: { هل تعلم له سميا } مثلا، فتلتفت إليه وتقبل بوجهك نحوه فيفيض عليك مطلوبك

BIQAI-FULL:v4p549/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p549/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p549/r3.claim: After establishing God’s command and encompassing knowledge, the text names him Lord of the heavens, earth, and all beings between them, making the case for resurrection more explicit and comprehensive.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p549/r3.anchor: ولما وصف سبحانه وتعالى بنفوذ الأمر واتساع العلم على وجه ثبت به ما أخبر به عن الجنة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p549/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p549/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p549/r4.claim: Worship God with continual vigilance and endure its demands with full effort, since worship entails severe striving.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p549/r4.anchor: أي اصبر صبرا عظيما بغاية جهدك

BIQAI-FULL:v4p549/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p549/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p549/r5.claim: Samiy means one truly sharing any divine attribute or even bearing God’s name; the rhetorical question argues that he has no counterpart.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p549/r5.anchor: لأنه لا مماثل له حتى ولا في مجرد الاسم

DURR-FULL:v5p531/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p531/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p531/r3.claim: He interprets whether God has a namesake as asking whether He has any equal or likeness.
DURR-FULL:v5p531/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {هل تعلم له سميا} قال: هل تعلم للرب مثلا أو شبها

DURR-FULL:v5p531/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p531/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p531/r4.claim: He says no one besides God is named al-Rahman.
DURR-FULL:v5p531/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {هل تعلم له سميا} قال: ليس أحد يسمى الرحمن غيره

DURR-FULL:v5p531/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p531/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p531/r5.claim: He explains the address as asking Muhammad whether he knows of a child for his God.
DURR-FULL:v5p531/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه في قوله: {هل تعلم له سميا} يا محمد هل تعلم لإلهك من ولد

DURR-FULL:v5p531/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p531/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p531/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas also glosses the word as a child and cites poetry to attest this Arabic usage.
DURR-FULL:v5p531/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: أن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قوله: {هل تعلم له سميا}

QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r16.claim: Since God brings things into existence and has power over them, He is their Lord and owner; an act belongs to its agent insofar as its existence lies within its power.
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r16.anchor: وإذا وجدت فهو فاعلها ، فمعنى كون فعل الشيء لفاعله

QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r17.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r17.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r17.claim: If God is Lord of powerful great ones, He is also Lord of the small and weak; a servant's value derives from the owner, not intrinsic status.
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r17.anchor: وقيمة العبد بمالكه وقدره ، لا بثمنه في نفسه وخطره

QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r18.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r18.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r18.claim: Worship means standing wherever God commands and relinquishing personal inclination, opinion, and planning.
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r18.anchor: قف حيثما أمرك ، ودع ما يقع لك ، وخل رأيك وتدبيرك

QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r19.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r19.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r19.claim: To persevere in worship is to reach the utmost limit of patience.

QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r20.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r20.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r20.claim: God has no namesake in the sense of an equal or peer; no one else bears the name Allah, and none can resemble Him in pre-eternity.
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r20.anchor: هل تعلم له سميا } : أي كفوا ونظيرا

QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r21.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r21.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r21.claim: God has no likeness, whether existent or merely imagined; resemblance would imply equality.
QUSHAYRI:v2p244/r21.anchor: والتشبيه يقتضي التسوية بين المتشابهين ، ولا مثل له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r1.claim: The verse begins a new divine address to the Prophet, concluding that angels act only by their Lord’s leave and all creation is under God’s control, then commanding worship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r1.anchor: من كلام الله تعالى كما يقتضيه قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r2.claim: “Lord of the heavens” is the predicate of an omitted subject; usage requires omitting it when a final distinguishing description follows other descriptions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r2.anchor: على الخبرية لمبتدأ محذوف ملتزم الحذف في المقام الذي يذكر فيه أحد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r3.claim: A verse attributed uncertainly to al-Ṣūlī or Ibn al-Zubayr illustrates the omitted subject before a final predicate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r3.anchor: كقول الصولي أو ابن الزبير بفتح الزاي وكسر الموحدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r4.claim: The heavens are upper worlds, earth the lower world, and what lies between them the skies and horizons; together the three cover all beings.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r5.claim: The worship and patience commands address the Prophet, derive naturally from God’s universal control, and transition to affirming monotheism while condemning association.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r5.anchor: والخطاب في { فاعبده واصطبر } و { هل تعلم } للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r6.claim: Iṣṭibār is intense patience; although normally followed by ʿalā, the lām here conveys steadfastness because worship includes varied struggles of self-mastery.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r6.anchor: والاصطبار : شدة الصبر على الأمر الشاق ، لأن صيغة الافتعال ترد لإفادة قوة الفعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r7.speaker: النبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r7.claim: The Prophet says the ʿishāʾ prayer is the heaviest prayer for hypocrites, illustrating why worship requires firmness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p141/r7.anchor: كما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في صلاة العشاء : ( هي أثقل صلاة على المنافقين )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p143/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p143/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p143/r1.claim: The rhetorical question about whether anyone is God’s samiyy explains why He alone deserves worship and why the Prophet should persevere.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p143/r1.anchor: وجملة { هل تعلم له سميا } واقعة موقع التعليل للأمر بعبادته والاصطبار عليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p143/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p143/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p143/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets samiyy as a counterpart or equal, derived from musāmāh; Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers this sense, which means comparable in all attributes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p143/r2.anchor: فعن ابن عباس أنه فسره بالنظير ، مأخوذا من المساماة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p143/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p143/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p143/r3.claim: On the preferred sense, the interrogative is a denial: no being exists who equals or resembles God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p143/r3.anchor: والاستفهام إنكاري ، أي لا مسامي لله تعالى ، أي ليس من يساميه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p143/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p143/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p143/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes samiyy as someone with the same name, like the description of John in 19:7; no idol is called “Allah,” and their failure to claim creative power acknowledges God’s uniqueness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p143/r4.anchor: المماثل في الاسم . كقوله في ذكر يحيى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p143/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p143/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p143/r5.claim: The alternate reading also grounds exclusive worship: people do not know a namesake, and the absence of a known equal entails that no other being deserves worship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p143/r5.anchor: وكني بانتفاء العلم بسميه عن انتفاء وجود سمي له ، لأن العلم يستلزم وجود المعلوم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r11.claim: Rabb is in apposition to the preceding “your Lord”; worship and steadfastness command bearing the demanding legal obligations.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p24/r11.anchor: وقوله رب بدل من قوله وما كان ربك، وقوله فاعبده واصطبر لعبادته أمر بحمل تكاليف الشرع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r1.claim: Most pronounce the lām in hal taʿlam clearly; Ali ibn Nasr from Abu Amr and several others assimilate it into tāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «هل تعلم» بإظهار اللام، وقرأ علي بن نصر عن أبي عمرو بإدغام اللام في التاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r2.claim: Sibawayh allows lām assimilation into several following consonants; Abu Amr also assimilates into thāʾ in wa-hal thūwiba, though tāʾ is the closer articulation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي: سيبويه يجيز إدغام اللام في الطاء والتاء والدال والثاء والضاد والزاي والسين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r3.speaker: مزاحم العقيلي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r3.claim: Al-Muzahim al-Uqayli's verse illustrates assimilation of lām into tāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r3.anchor:
ومن إدغامها في التاء ما روي من قول مزاحم العقيلي: [الطويل]
فذر ذا ولكن هل تعين متيما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r4.claim: One interpretation takes samiyyan literally as sharing a name with the Lord of the heavens and earth; no people name an idol or other being with this unique title.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r4.anchor: وقوله سميا، قال قوم: وهو ظاهر اللفظ معناه موافقا في الاسم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and others interpret samiyyan as an equal, likeness, or peer; Ibn Atiyya approves this as a good reading here.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغيره: قوله سميا معناه مثيلا أو شبيها أو نحو ذلك، وهذا قول حسن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r6.claim: This peer-like sense derives samī from musāmī/muḍāhī; it fits this verse, but not the earlier mention of John.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p25/r6.anchor: وكأن السمي بمعنى المسامي والمضاهي فهو من السمو، وهذا القول يحسن في هذه الآية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r1.claim: Worship God alone, since worship mixed with association is not truly worship; persevere either in His oneness or in His commands and prohibitions.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r1.anchor: فاعبده أي وحده لأن عبادته بالشرك ليست عبادة واصطبر لعبادته أي اصبر على توحيده

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r2.speaker: هارون عن أبي عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r2.claim: Abu ʿAmr assimilates the lām of هل into ت in هل تعلم.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r2.anchor: روى هارون عن أبي عمرو أنه كان يدغم هل تعلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r3.speaker: سيبويه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r3.claim: Sibawayh permits assimilating lām into several following consonants because their articulation points are close.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r3.anchor: أن سيبويه يجيز إدغام اللام في التاء والثاء والدال والزاي والسين والصاد والطاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r4.claim: When هل is followed by ت, some speakers pronounce the lām distinctly and others assimilate it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r4.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة إذا كان بعد هل تاء ففيه لغتان بعضهم يبين لام هل وبعضهم يدغمها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r5.claim: One meaning of samiyyan is an equal or likeness; Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, and Qatadah agree.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r5.anchor: مثلا وشبها رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس وبه قال سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r6.claim: Another meaning asks whether anyone besides God is called Allah.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r6.anchor: هل تعلم أحدا يسمى الله غيره رواه عطاء عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj reads it as asking whether anyone besides God deserves to be called Creator and Powerful.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p251/r7.anchor: هل تعلم أحدا يستحق أن يقال له خالق وقادر الا هو قاله الزجاج

SULAMI:v1p431#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p431#2/r1.speaker: محمد بن الفضل
SULAMI:v1p431#2/r1.claim: No one but God answers whenever you call and receives you whenever you turn to Him.
SULAMI:v1p431#2/r1.anchor: قال محمد بن الفضل : هل تعلم أحد يجيبك في أي وقت دعوته ويقبلك في أي أوان قصدته

SULAMI:v1p431#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p431#2/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
SULAMI:v1p431#2/r2.claim: None is named Allah except Allah Himself.
SULAMI:v1p431#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين : تعلم أحدا يسمى الله إلا الله

SULAMI:v1p431#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p431#2/r3.speaker: الحسين ابن الفضل
SULAMI:v1p431#2/r3.claim: No one else deserves to be called by one of God’s real names.
SULAMI:v1p431#2/r3.anchor: وقال الحسين ابن الفضل : هل تستحق أحدا أن يسمى باسم من أسمائه الحقيقية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p250/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p250/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p250/r1.claim: Calling God Lord of the heavens and earth means He created, governs, rules, and disposes of them, with no one able to overturn His decree.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p250/r1.anchor: [أي: خالق ذلك ومدبره، والحاكم فيه والمتصرف الذي لا معقب لحكمه، {فاعبده واصطبر لعبادته] (7)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p250/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p250/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p250/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Qatada, Ibn Jurayj, and others interpret God's namesake as an equal or likeness.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p250/r2.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: هل تعلم للرب مثلا أو شبها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p250/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p250/r3.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p250/r3.claim: ʿIkrima transmits Ibn ʿAbbas's view that no one besides God is named al-Rahman.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p250/r3.anchor: وقال عكرمة، عن ابن عباس: ليس أحد يسمى الرحمن غيره تبارك وتعالى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r13.claim: On that alternative, God confirms that He does not forget workers' deeds, then the Prophet is told to worship and work so God may reward him like the pious.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p30#2/r13.anchor: فحين عرفته على هذه الصفة ، فأقبل على العمل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r1.claim: “Lord of the heavens and earth” either apposes “your Lord” or predicates an omitted “He is.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r1.anchor: بدل من ربك ، ويجوز أن يكون خبر مبتدأ محذوف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r2.claim: On the second parsing, “worship Him” has the construction illustrated by the cited line about marrying the women of Khawlān.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r3.claim: With that parsing, “your Lord was not forgetful” may be the pious speaking, while the following words are God's speech.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r3.anchor: وما بعده من كلام رب العزة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r4.claim: “Persevere for His worship” takes lām rather than the usual ʿalā because worship is treated like an opponent in battle whom one must withstand.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r4.anchor: لأن العبادة جعلت بمنزلة القرن في قولك للمحارب : اصطبر لقرنك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r5.claim: Worship brings hardships, so remain firm and do not lose heart at scriptural sophistries, delayed revelation, or the polytheists' gloating.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r6.claim: No thing is truly named Allah; unlike idols called gods, this name belongs uniquely to the true deity.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says no one besides God is called al-Raḥmān.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r8.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r8.claim: Alternatively, no one bears His name truthfully; a false naming counts as no naming at all.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r8.anchor: هل تعلم من سمي باسمه على الحق دون الباطل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r9.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r9.claim: Samiyy may mean peer or likeness; since only God is worthy of worship, worship and perseverance are necessary.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p31#2/r9.anchor: مثلا وشبيها ، أي : إذا صح أن لا معبود

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r8.claim: Samiyyan may mean a peer or likeness, from mutual exaltation; Mujahid shares this.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r8.anchor: يعني مثلا وشبيها , قاله ابن عباس , ومجاهد , مأخوذ من المساماة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r9.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r9.claim: No one besides God is called by the divine name; al-Kalbi agrees.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r9.anchor: أنه لا أحد يسمى بالله غيره , قاله قتادة , والكلبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r10.claim: Another interpretation asks whether anyone deserves to be called a god besides Him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r10.anchor: الثالث : أنه لا يستحق أحد أن يسمى إلها غيره . الرابع

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r11.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r11.claim: Samiyyan may mean a son; Abu Talib's poem is cited with the related word musamma.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p381/r11.anchor: هل تعلم له من ولد , قاله الضحاك , قال أبو طالب

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p382/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p382/r1.speaker: أبو طالب
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p382/r1.claim: The cited poem uses musamma in connection with the meaning of samiyyan.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p382/r1.anchor: أما المسمى فأنت منه مكثر … لكنه ما للخلود سبيل

MUQATIL:19:61-65/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:61-65/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:61-65/r7.claim: The Lord of the heavens, earth, and all creatures is to be worshipped as one; the Prophet should patiently persist without haste. God has no namesake among the deities, since He prevents people from calling another god Allah.
MUQATIL:19:61-65/r7.anchor: يقول: واصبر على توحيد الله عز وجل ولا تعجل حتى يأتيك أمري

NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#4/r1.claim: رب السماوات may be appositional to ربك or the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning He is Lord of the heavens and earth.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#4/r1.anchor: بدل من ربك أو خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي هو رب السموات

NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#4/r2.claim: Since the Messenger knows these divine attributes, he is commanded to worship God and remain constant in worship.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#4/r2.anchor: ثم قال لرسوله لما عرفت أنه متصف بهذه الصفات

NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#4/r3.claim: اصطبر means endure the hardship and envy encountered in worship so as to continue performing it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#4/r3.anchor: أي اصبر على مكافأة الحسود لعبادة المعبود واصر على المشاق لاجل عبادة الخلاق أي لتتمكن من الاتيان بها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#4/r4.claim: سَمِيّ may mean a likeness or equal, or ask whether anyone besides God bears His name; only He is the true deity, so worship and perseverance belong to Him alone.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p42#4/r4.anchor: شبيها ومثلا أو هل يسمى أحد باسم الله غيره لأن مخصوص بالمعبود بالحق

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p272#5/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p272#5/r2.speaker: المفسرون
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p272#5/r2.claim: Exegetes take samiyyan in 19:65 to mean a likeness or counterpart.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p272#5/r2.anchor: {هل تعلم له سميا} فإنه أراد - فيما ذكر المفسرون - شبيها

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p272#5/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p272#5/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p272#5/r3.claim: He also considers it plausible that 19:65 means no one else is named by God's name.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p272#5/r3.anchor: ولو أراد أنه لا يسمي الله غيره، كان وجها.

MAJAZ:v2p8/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p8/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p8/r6.claim: سميّا means an equal or counterpart.
MAJAZ:v2p8/r6.anchor: «هل تعلم له سميا» (65) هل تعرف له نظيرا ومثلا

MAJAZ:v2p8/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p8/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p8/r7.claim: After هل, Arabs either pronounce the lām before tāʾ or assimilate it, saying هتعلم because two consecutive tāʾs are heavy.
MAJAZ:v2p8/r7.anchor: إذا كان بعد هل تاء ففيها لغتان فبعضهم يبين لام «هل» وبعضهم يخمدها فيقول: «هتعلم»

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r8.claim: God is master and creator of heaven, earth, and all between them; therefore worship Him alone and persist patiently in obedience rather than grieve over delayed revelation.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r8.anchor: { رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما } أي ربهما وخالقهما وخالق ما بينهما ومالكهما ومالك ما بينهما

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r9.claim: The verse proves human acquisitions are created by God: since He owns everything, He alone deserves worship, defined as obedience with utmost humility.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r9.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أن اكتسابات الخلق مفعولة لله تعالى كما يقوله أهل الحق، وهو القول الحق

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r10.claim: Iṣṭabir derives from iṣtabir; the difficult t-ṣ cluster changes t to ṭ, as in the form derived from ṣawm.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r10.anchor: وأصل اصطبر اصتبر، فثقل الجمع بين التاء والصاد لاختلافهما، فأبدل من التاء طاء كما تقول من الصوم: اصطام

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r11.claim: They explain samiyyan as a child, rival, likeness, or one worthy to share the name al-Rahman, deriving the term from mutual elevation.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد هل تعلم له ولدا أو نظيرا أو مثلا أو شبيها يستحق مثل اسمه الذي هو الرحمن.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r12.claim: A report through Israil, Simak, and Ikrima asks whether anyone besides God is named al-Rahman; al-Nahhas calls it the strongest known chain and a sound view.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r12.anchor: وروى إسرائيل عن سماك عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال: هل تعلم أحدا سمي الرحمن.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r13.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r13.anchor: روى ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد «هل تعلم له سميا» قال: مثلا.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r14.speaker: ابن المسيب
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r14.claim: Ibn al-Musayyib glosses samiyyan as an equal.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r15.speaker: قتادة والكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r15.claim: Qatada and al-Kalbi read the question as asking whether anyone is called Allah besides God; the interrogative means no.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:64-65#2/r15.anchor: قتادة والكلبي: هل تعلم أحدا يسمي الله تعالى غير الله، أو يقال له الله إلا الله. وهل بمعنى لا

RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r2.claim: The Lord of the heavens and earth cannot forget, since He must continuously sustain them or their order and all dependent existence would collapse.
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r2.anchor: فالمراد أن من يكون ربا لها أجمع لا يجوز عليه النسيان إذ لا بد من أن يمسكها حالا بعد حال

RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r3.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r3.claim: The author’s school uses God’s lordship over everything between heaven and earth to argue that human acts are created by God.
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r3.anchor: واحتج / أصحابنا بهذه الآية على أن فعل العبد خلق الله تعالى ، لأن فعل العبد حاصل بين السماء والأرض

RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r4.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses “Lord of the heavens and earth” either as an apposition to “your Lord” or as the predicate of an omitted “He is.”
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r4.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : رب السموات والأرض بدل من ربك ويجوز أن يكون خبر مبتدأ محذوف

RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r5.claim: The command directs Muhammad to worship and persevere through the hardships of religious duties, conveying the message, and his own worship despite sophistries and mockery over delayed revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r5.anchor: فهو أمر للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بالعبادة والمصابرة على مشاق التكاليف في الأداء والإبلاغ

RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r6.claim: “Persevere for His worship” uses li rather than ‘ala because worship is like an opponent a fighter must withstand; worship brings hardship, so one must stay firm.
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r6.anchor: لأن العبادة جعلت بمنزلة القرن في قولك للمحارب اصطبر لقرنك أي اثبت له فيما يورد عليك من شداته

RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r7.claim: The author reads “Do you know anyone like Him?” as grounding worship and perseverance in God’s uniqueness and incomparable beneficence through creating bodies, life, intellect, and other fundamental blessings.
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r7.anchor: والأقرب هو كونه منعما بأصول النعم وفروعها وهي خلق الأجسام والحياة والعقل وغيرها

RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r8.claim: Another interpretation says God has no namesake or partner in His name; idols may be called gods, but no one else is called Allah, and Ibn Abbas says no one else is called al-Rahman.
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r8.anchor: ومن الناس من قال : المراد أنه سبحانه ليس له شريك في اسمه وبينوا ذلك من وجهين

RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says no one besides God is named al-Rahman.
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r9.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما لا يسمى بالرحمن غيره

RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r10.claim: The author rejects the namesake-only explanation and says the more sound meaning is that no one shares God’s unique creative beneficence, which obligates supreme worship.
RAZI-FULL:v21p205/r10.anchor: والقول الأول هو الصواب والله أعلم

STUDYQURAN:19:65/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:65/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:65/r1.claim: Lord of the heavens and the earth is a Quranic title for God.
STUDYQURAN:19:65/r1.anchor: Lord of the heavens and the earth is a title for God found also

STUDYQURAN:19:65/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:65/r2.speaker: Ṭabarī
STUDYQURAN:19:65/r2.claim: The closing question may ask whether anyone equals God in generosity and bounty, or whether any partner can be named beside Him.
STUDYQURAN:19:65/r2.anchor: Is there any who is His equal or His like in generosity and bounty

STUDYQURAN:19:65/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:65/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:65/r3.claim: The question is rhetorical: no one besides God should be called God and idols are not gods; some commentators say none besides Him should be called al-Raḥmān.
STUDYQURAN:19:65/r3.anchor: indicating that no one should be called

NAHHAS:v3p21/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p21/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p21/r13.claim: The underlying form is اصتبر; the tāʾ-ṣād cluster is heavy, so tāʾ becomes ṭāʾ, as in اصطام from الصوم.
NAHHAS:v3p21/r13.anchor: الأصل اصتبر فثقل الجمع بين التاء والصاد لاختلافهما

TAB-FULL:v15p585/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p585/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p585/r1.claim: “Lord of the heavens and earth” restates “your Lord”: were He forgetful, creation would not endure and would perish without His preservation.

TAB-FULL:v15p585/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p585/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p585/r2.claim: Worship means persist in obedience and submit to God’s commands and prohibitions; patience in worship means holding oneself to obey, seeking His approval.

TAB-FULL:v15p585/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p585/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p585/r3.claim: The rhetorical question asks whether the Lord has any namesake, equal, or likeness in generosity; none exists, so He alone is worshipped for His favor.
TAB-FULL:v15p585/r3.anchor: هل تعلم يا محمد لربك هذا الذي أمرناك بعبادته، والصبر على طاعته مثلا في كرمه وجوده

TAB-FULL:v15p585/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p585/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p585/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses samiyyan as an example or likeness of the Lord.
TAB-FULL:v15p585/r4.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {هل تعلم له سميا} [مريم: 65] يقول: هل تعلم للرب مثلا أو شبيها

TAB-FULL:v15p585/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p585/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p585/r5.claim: A second report attributed to Ibn ʿAbbas likewise glosses it as a likeness.
TAB-FULL:v15p585/r5.anchor: عن الحسن بن عمارة، عن رجل، عن ابن عباس في قوله {هل تعلم له سميا} [مريم: 65] قال: شبيها

TAB-FULL:v15p585/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p585/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p585/r6.claim: Mujahid explains the question as asking whether God has a likeness or example.
TAB-FULL:v15p585/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، في هذه الآية {هل تعلم له سميا} [مريم: 65] قال: هل تعلم له شبيها، هل تعلم له مثلا

TAB-FULL:v15p585/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p585/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p585/r7.claim: Qatada says God has no namesake or equal, and every creature acknowledges Him as creator; he cites 43:87.
TAB-FULL:v15p585/r7.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {هل تعلم له سميا} [مريم: 65] لا سمي لله ولا عدل له، كل خلقه يقر له

TAB-FULL:v15p585/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p585/r8.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v15p585/r8.claim: Ibn Jurayj interprets the phrase as denying God any partner or likeness.
TAB-FULL:v15p585/r8.anchor: عن ابن جريج، في قوله: {هل تعلم له سميا} [مريم: 65] قال: يقول: لا شريك له ولا مثل

TABATABAI:19:64-65/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:64-65/r1.claim: These two verses interrupt the surrounding passage, yet their Qur’anic style indicates that they are Gabriel’s speech revealed by God; this supports reports that the Prophet asked why Gabriel’s coming was delayed and received this reply by revelation.
TABATABAI:19:64-65/r1.anchor: سياقهما يشهد بأنهما من كلام ملك الوحي بوحي قرآني من الله سبحانه

TABATABAI:19:64-65/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:19:64-65/r2.claim: Reports, including one attributed to Ibn ʿAbbas in al-Majmaʿ, say the Prophet found Gabriel’s revelation delayed and asked him about it.
TABATABAI:19:64-65/r2.anchor: ورواه في مجمع البيان أيضا عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم استبطأ نزول جبريل

TABATABAI:19:64-65/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:19:64-65/r3.claim: The author rejects proposed links that insert an implied statement by Gabriel, connect the verses to Gabriel’s earlier words to Mary, or put them in the mouths of the pious in Paradise; context and eloquence disfavor them.
TABATABAI:19:64-65/r3.anchor: وهي جميعا وجوه ظاهرة السخافة يأباها السياق ولا يقبلها النظم البليغ

TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r1.claim: Calling God Lord of the heavens, earth, and all between them explains His ownership and unfailing governance, since lordship entails ownership and managing affairs.

TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r2.claim: The command to worship and persevere follows because the message is God’s own call: worship Him alone, since there is no other lord to replace Him or share worship.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r2.anchor: فالكلام كلامه والدعوة دعوته فاعبده وحده واصطبر لعبادته

TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r3.claim: The author rejects making worship and perseverance follow directly from the phrase Lord of the heavens or from God not being forgetful; those links do not fit the argument.

TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r4.claim: The question about a namesake completes the rationale for worship: no one shares the name Lord and its universal, absolute lordship so as to merit worship instead.

TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r5.claim: Samiyy means one sharing the name Lord, because the argument establishes God’s absolute lordship over everything.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r5.anchor: المراد بالسمي المشارك في الاسم والمراد بالاسم هو الرب لأن مقتضى بيان الآية

TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r6.claim: The author rejects glosses of samiyy as a figurative equal, a child, or as a shared proper name meaning God, Allah, deity, al-Rahman, or the creator and giver of life and death.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r6.anchor: فقد قيل إن المراد بالسمي المماثل مجازا

TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r7.claim: Repeatedly addressing the angels’ speaker as your Lord prepares the declaration of oneness: the angels’ Lord is the Prophet’s Lord, so the call to worship is His; the surah’s opening has the same coherent aim.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r7.anchor: إشارة إلى أن ربنا الذي نتنزل عن أمره هو ربك

TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r8.claim: Worship and perseverance express unity of worship; remaining constant in worship is implied by, rather than a separate sense beyond, the command to worship.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#3/r8.anchor: مسوق لتوحيد العبادة وليس أمرا بالعبادة وأمرا بالثبات عليها وإدامتها إلا من جهة الملازمة

TABATABAI:19:64-65#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:64-65#4/r1.claim: The proposed continuation makes the two verses confirm the preceding revelation: Gabriel was commanded to deliver the surah and then clarify that he descended only by God’s command, whose call is to worship the sole Lord.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#4/r1.anchor: فكأن ملك الوحي لما تنزل عليه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بالسورة وأوحى إليه الآيات الثلاث والستين

TABATABAI:19:64-65#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:64-65#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:64-65#4/r2.claim: The king-and-messenger analogy shows how Gabriel’s explanatory words remain a message from God; this reading fits the verses better and more clearly than varying, weak occasion reports.
TABATABAI:19:64-65#4/r2.anchor: وهذا نظير أن يرسل ملك رسولا بكتاب من عنده أو رسالة إلى بعض عماله

TABRISI:19:61-65/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:61-65/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
TABRISI:19:61-65/r2.claim: In some transmissions from Abū ʿAmr the lām of hal taʿlam assimilates into the tāʾ; most pronounce it distinctly.
TABRISI:19:61-65/r2.anchor: وفي بعض الروايات عن أبي عمرو هل تعلم يدغم اللام في التاء

TABRISI:19:61-65/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:61-65/r4.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:19:61-65/r4.claim: Sībawayh permits assimilating lām into nearby tongue-tip consonants; al-ʿUqaylī's line illustrates it.
TABRISI:19:61-65/r4.anchor: قال أبو علي يرى سيبويه أن إدغام اللام في التاء والدال والطاء والصاد والزاي والسين جائز

TABRISI:19:61-65/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:61-65/r9.speaker: الأخفش
TABRISI:19:61-65/r9.claim: Rabb al-samāwāti may be apposition to kāna's predicate or a new clause whose predicate is faʿbudhu; the latter follows al-Akhfash, not Sībawayh.
TABRISI:19:61-65/r9.anchor: وإن شئت كان مبتدأ وقوله: { فاعبده } خبره وهذا على قول الأخفش دون سيبويه

TABRISI:19:65/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:65/r1.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:19:65/r1.claim: God does not forget anyone and so fail to resurrect that person.
TABRISI:19:65/r1.anchor: وقيل: ما كان ربك ناسيا لأحد حتى لا يبعثه يوم القيامة عن أبي مسلم

TABRISI:19:65/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:65/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:65/r2.claim: God is creator and governor of the heavens and earth; worship Him alone and patiently endure worship's demands.
TABRISI:19:65/r2.anchor: { رب السماوات والأرض } أي خالقهما ومدبرهما

TABRISI:19:65/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:65/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وابن جريج وسعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:19:65/r3.claim: The question asks whether God has any likeness or equal.
TABRISI:19:65/r3.anchor: { هل تعلم له سميا } أي مثلا وشبيها عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:19:65/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:65/r4.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:19:65/r4.claim: Another interpretation asks whether anyone but God deserves to be called a deity.
TABRISI:19:65/r4.anchor: وقيل: هل تعلم أحدا يستحق أن يسمى إلها إلا هو عن الكلبي

TABRISI:19:65/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:65/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:65/r5.claim: A further explanation asks if anyone else is deity, creator, provider, giver and taker of life, or able to reward and punish; the rhetorical answer is no.
TABRISI:19:65/r5.anchor: هل تعلم أحدا يسمى إلها خالقا رازقا محييا مميتا قادرا على الثواب والعقاب

THALABI:v6p223/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p223/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p223/r4.claim: The verse commands worship and patient perseverance in worship of the Lord of the heavens and earth.

THALABI:v6p223/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p223/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p223/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses samiyyan as an equal or counterpart to God.

THALABI:v6p223/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p223/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v6p223/r6.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr glosses samiyyan as a match.

THALABI:v6p223/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p223/r7.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v6p223/r7.claim: Al-Kalbi reads the question as asking whether anyone besides God is called Allah.
THALABI:v6p223/r7.anchor: وقال الكلبي: هل تعلم أحدا يسمى الله غيره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r1.claim: God is owner of the heavens, earth, and their creatures; worship Him alone, since worship joined with idolatry is no worship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {قال رب السماوات والأرض} أي: مالكهما {وما بينهما}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r2.claim: Persist in worship means persist in obeying God.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r3.claim: Another explanation is to be patient with God’s commands and prohibitions.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير وابن جريج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r4.claim: A namesake means an equal or likeness to God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r4.anchor: قال في # رواية الوالبي: (هل تعلم للرب مثلا أو شبها)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r5.claim: In Simak’s narration, the question asks whether anyone besides God is named al-Rahman; Ibn Masʿud’s reading supports this.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r5.anchor: وقال في رواية سماك: (هل تعلم أحدا اسمه الرحمن غيره)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r6.claim: His reading makes the question: al-Rahman, do you know anyone named like Him?
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r6.anchor: ودليل هذا القول قراءة ابن مسعود: (الرحمن هل تعلم له سميا).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r7.claim: In Ata’s narration, it asks whether anyone besides God is called Allah.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r7.anchor: وقال في رواية عطاء: (هل تعلم أحدا يسمى الله غيره)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r8.claim: A true namesake would deserve the attributes Creator, Powerful, and knowing all past and future; only God does, so no one deserves any of His names.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r8.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (تأويله -والله أعلم- هل تعلم له سميا يستحق أن يقال له: خالق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r9.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r9.claim: No one is called Allah except God; idolaters attempted related names, calling an idol al-Lat and al-ʿAziz al-ʿUzza.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p282#2/r9.anchor: وقال مقاتل: (لا يسمى باسم الله غير الله، لما حاول المشركون التسمية بالله قالوا: اللات

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:63-66/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:63-66/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:63-66/r6.claim: A namesake would be someone else named God; no one else is called by that name.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:63-66/r6.anchor: هل تعلم له سميا } هل تعلم أحدا يسمى الله غيره؟

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r6.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r6.claim: Qatāda interprets whether God has a namesake as asking whether He has an equal.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r6.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: هل تعلم له عدلا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r7.speaker: يحيى
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r7.claim: Yaḥyā explains the question through the idea of being comparable or sharing a rank.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r7.anchor: قال يحيى: أي من قبل المساماة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r8.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says the names Allah and al-Raḥmān are reserved names no creature could claim for itself.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r8.anchor: أبو الأشهب، عن الحسن قال: الله والرحمن اسمان ممنوعان لم يستطع أحد من الخلق أن ينتحلهما

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r9.claim: The rhetorical question means that no one knows of any namesake equal to God.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p234/r9.anchor: على الاستفهام، أي إنك لا تعلمه

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r5.claim: Semiyy can mean similar, but the author prefers worthy to bear His name: Arabs reserved the name Allah for God and called idols ilāh.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r5.anchor: “Adını almaya lâyık” diye çevirdiğimiz semiyy kelimesi, “benzer” mânasına da gelir. Bizim de tercih ettiğimiz birinci mânaya göre Allah ismi, yüce yaratıcı olan Cenâb-ı Hak’tan başkasına verilmemiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r6.claim: On the alternative meaning of semiyy as similar, the verse denies that God has any equal and therefore denies that anything besides Him deserves worship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:64/r6.anchor: İkinci mânaya göre âyet, Allah’ın eşi ve benzerinin bulunmadığını, dolayısıyla ondan başka hiçbir şeyin ibadet edilmeye lâyık olmadığını belirtir

SAMIN-DURR:19:65/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:65/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:65/r1.claim: رب السماوات may be an apposition to ربك, a predicate of an omitted هو, or a subject whose predicate is the following imperative clause; the last parse follows al-Akhfash’s allowance of an extra fā’ in any predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:19:65/r1.anchor: قوله: { رب السماوات }: فيه ثلاثة أقوال، أحدها: كونه بدلا من " ربك ". الثاني: كونه خبر مبتدأ، أي: هو رب.

SAMIN-DURR:19:65/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:65/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:65/r2.claim: لعبادته depends on اصطبر; although the verb normally takes على, it is framed with the sense ‘remain steadfast,’ since few persist through worship’s many demands.
SAMIN-DURR:19:65/r2.anchor: قوله: لعبادته " متعلق ب " اصطبر " وكان من حقه تعديته ب " على " لأنها صلته

SAMIN-DURR:19:65/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:65/r3.speaker: الأخوان، هشام
SAMIN-DURR:19:65/r3.claim: The two readers and Hisham, along with others, assimilate the lām of هل into the tā’ of تعلم.
SAMIN-DURR:19:65/r3.anchor: قوله: " هل تعلم " أدغم الأخوان وهشام وجماعة لام " هل " في التاء،

SAMIN-DURR:19:65/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:65/r4.speaker: مزاحم العقيلي
SAMIN-DURR:19:65/r4.claim: They cite a line by Muzahim al-‘Uqayli as evidence for the assimilation.
SAMIN-DURR:19:65/r4.anchor: وأنشدوا على ذلك بيت مزاحم العقيلي.

ZAJJAJ:v3p338/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p338/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p338/r1.claim: The Lord owns the heavens and earth and knows them and everything in them.
ZAJJAJ:v3p338/r1.anchor: أي هو مالك لهما وعالم بهما وبما فيهما

ZAJJAJ:v3p338/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p338/r2.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v3p338/r2.claim: The exegesis glosses سميّا as “a likeness” and also says only God has been named al-Raḥmān.
ZAJJAJ:v3p338/r2.anchor: جاء في التفسير: هل تعلم له مثلا، وجاء أيضا لم يسم بالرحمن إلا الله عز وجل.

ZAJJAJ:v3p338/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p338/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p338/r3.claim: No one but God merits the titles Creator, Powerful, and Knower of past and future.
ZAJJAJ:v3p338/r3.anchor: يستحق أن يقال له خالق وقادر وعالم بما كان وبما يكون

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p203/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p203/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p203/r1.claim: Abu Amr is reported both to assimilate the lām in هل تعلم and to articulate it; Harun says he later returned to clear pronunciation.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p203/r1.anchor: علي بن نصر عن أبي عمرو: هل تعلم له [مريم/ 65] يدغم اللام ويقول: إن شئت أدغمته،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p203/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p203/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p203/r2.claim: Sibawayh permits assimilating lām into tip-of-tongue consonants; assimilation into tāʾ is supported by Abu Amr's هل ثوب and بل تؤثرون readings.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p203/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي: يرى سيبويه: أن إدغام اللام في الطاء والدال والتاء والصاد والزاي والسين جائز،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p203/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p203/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p203/r3.claim: A line by Muzahim al-Uqayli with هتعين exemplifies assimilation of lām into tāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p203/r3.anchor: وأنشد لمزاحم العقيلي: فذر ذا ولكن هتعين متيما ... على ضوء برق آخر الليل ناصب

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p236/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p236/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p236/r4.claim: Samiyyan may mean no one before bore the same name, or that no child had been born to his parents before him; the later question about a namesake allows both senses.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p236/r4.anchor: قيل لم يسم باسمه غيره وقيل لم يولد لأبويه ولد قبله

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p238/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p238/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p238/r4.claim: Hal taʿlamu may be assimilated because the sounds are close, or pronounced clearly according to the original separation of its consonants.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p238/r4.anchor: يقرأ بالإدغام للمقاربة وبالإظهار على الأصل وانفصال الحرفين

IBNMUJAHID:v1p409/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p409/r5.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p409/r5.claim: ʿAlī b. Naṣr reports Abū ʿAmr assimilating lām in hal taʿlam, while allowing either assimilation or clear pronunciation; Hārūn says he later returned to clear pronunciation.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r1.claim: رب السماوات is parsed either as an apposition or as the predicate of an omitted subject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r1.anchor: وارتفع رب السماوات على البدل أو على خبر مبتدأ محذوف.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r2.claim: The majority pronounce the lām of هل تعلم distinctly before the tā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور هل تعلم بإظهار اللام عند التاء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r3.speaker: الأخوان، هشام، علي بن نصر، هارون عن أبي عمرو، الحسن، الأعمش، عيسى، ابن محيصن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r3.claim: These readers assimilate the lām in هل تعلم; Abu Ubayda calls the readings two dialects and cites Muzahim al-Uqayli, whose line witnesses تعين.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r3.anchor: وقرأ الأخوان وهشام وعلي بن نصر وهارون كلاهما عن أبي عمرو والحسن والأعمش وعيسى وابن محيصن بالإدغام فيهما.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda says the two pronunciations are both dialectal forms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r4.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: هما لغتان وعلى الإدغام أنشدوا بيت مزاحم العقيلي:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r5.claim: The lām in واصطبر لعبادته reflects semantic inclusion of steadfastness: worship entails hardships; the verb otherwise takes على, as in 20:132.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r5.anchor: وعدي فاصطبر باللام على سبيل التضمين أي اثبت بالصبر لعبادته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r6.claim: سمي can mean someone who shares a name; God alone is called Allah, though idolaters called idols gods and al-Uzza a god.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r6.anchor: والسمي من توافق في الاسم تقول: هذا سميك أي اسمه مثل اسمك،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says no one besides God is called الرحمن.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: لا يسمى أحد الرحمن غيره.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r8.claim: Another reading refers to Lord of the heavens and earth: no people name or describe anyone else with this designation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r8.anchor: وقيل: يحتمل أن يعود ذلك على قوله رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r9.speaker: مجاهد، ابن جبير، قتادة، ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r9.claim: They gloss سمي as equal or counterpart; Ibn Atiyya favors deriving it from elevation, meaning a peer or rival, but says that sense does not suit the verse about Yahya.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r9.anchor: وقال مجاهد وابن جبير وقتادة سميا مثلا وشبيها، وروي ذلك عن ابن عباس أيضا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r10.claim: Another distinction says سمي shares a name, while سميه matches fine qualities and merits; a poem contrasts sharing al-Zubayr's name with equaling him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r10.anchor: وقال غيره: يقال فلان سمي فلان إذا شاركه في اللفظ، وسميه إذا كان مماثلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r11.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r11.claim: Al-Zajjaj asks whether anyone besides God deserves the names Creator and Powerful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r11.anchor: وقال الزجاج: هل تعلم أحدا يستحق أن يقال له خالق وقادر إلا هو.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r12.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak takes سمي to mean a child, answering those who say God has offspring.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p283/r12.anchor: وقال الضحاك: ولدا ردا على من يقول ولد الله.

BURHAN:v4p436/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p436/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p436/r3.claim: The resumptive waw introduces an independent clause, not dependent in meaning or sharing a grammatical slot; it may introduce nominal or verbal clauses and prevents mistaking a clause for a single coordinated word.
BURHAN:v4p436/r3.anchor: واو الاستثناء وتسمى واو القطع والابتداء وهي التي يكون بعدها جملة غير متعلقة بما قبلها في المعنى

BURHAN:v2p5/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p5/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p5/r2.claim: An exegete must know legal theory because it is among the greatest means of deriving rulings from Qur’anic verses.
BURHAN:v2p5/r2.anchor: ولا بد من معرفة قواعد أصول الفقه فإنه من أعظم الطرق في استثمار الأحكام من الآيات

BURHAN:v2p5/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p5/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p5/r4.claim: An indefinite noun in an interrogative context is general: هل تعلم له سميا asks whether there is any namesake for God.
BURHAN:v2p5/r4.anchor: وفي الإستفهام من قوله ﴿ هل تعلم له سميا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p327/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p327/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p327/r1.claim: A single word cannot be divided so its act is literal but its inseparable result is metaphorical; unlike the distinct noun and derived verb in ‘God revived the earth.’
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p327/r1.anchor: ليس لك أن تجيء إلى لفظ امرين فتفرق دلالته وتجعله منقولا عن أصله في احدهما دون الآخر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p327/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p327/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p327/r2.claim: A metaphor can first transfer the source noun, as with ‘life,’ and then derive the verb ‘revive’ from that transferred sense.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p327/r2.anchor: أحدهما مشتق وهو أحيا والآخر مشتق منه وهو الحياة فنحن نقدر في المشتق منه أنه نقل عن معناه الأصلي

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p327/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p327/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p327/r3.claim: A noun’s annexation functions like a verb’s predication, so whatever literal or figurative judgment applies to a verbal noun’s annexation applies to verbal predication too.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p327/r3.anchor: الإضافة في الاسم كالإسناد في الفعل فكل حكم يجب في إضافة المصدر من حقيقة أو مجاز فهو واجب في إسناد الفعل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p327/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p327/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p327/r4.claim: Language cannot determine a genitive relation in isolation: annexation presupposes established usage and knowledge of which noun belongs with which complement.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p327/r4.anchor: الإضافة لا تكون حتى تستقر اللغة ويستحيل أن يكون للغة حكم في الإضافة ورسم حتى يعلم بها أن حق الاسم

DAMGHANI:v1p246/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p246/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p246/r9.claim: Samiyy can mean an equal or counterpart.
DAMGHANI:v1p246/r9.anchor: السادس : الاسم يعني المثل والعديل قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses samiyyan as a son, supported by a poetic line.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r1.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: ولدا، واستشهد بقول الشاعر: أما السمي فأنت منه مكثر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r2.claim: Bint al-Shati notes that although the Qur'an uses walad and awlād forty-six times, she finds no reading of samiyy as son in either Maryam verse.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r2.anchor: ولم اقف على تأويل "سميا" بولد، في آيتى مريم، كلتيهما

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r3.claim: In Arabic, one's samiyy is a namesake or counterpart; the related verbs can mean matching or competing, while simah is a mark and ism a distinguishing name.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r3.anchor: سَمِيُّكَ في اللغة: مَن اسمُه اسمُك ونظيرُك. وساماه باراه، وتساموا تباروا. والسمة العلامة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r4.claim: The word family appears widely: ism twenty-seven times, asmāʾ twelve, tasmiyah once, its verb forms eight times, and the passive participle musammā twenty-one times.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r4.anchor: ومن المادة جاء "اسم" سبعاً وعشرين مرة، وجمعه: أسماء، والأسماء اثنتى عشرة مرة و"تسمية" في آية النجم 23

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r5.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r5.claim: Al-Tabari, citing Ibn Abbas and others, interprets the question as asking whether God has an equal or likeness; none exists, and all creation acknowledges him as sole creator.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r5.anchor: وفي تأويل الطبري لآية مريم 65: هل تعلم يا محمد لربك مثلا أو شبيها: عن ابن عباس، وعن آخرين

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r6.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r6.claim: The cited interpretation denies any partner or peer for God and says every creature recognizes him as its creator.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r6.anchor: لا سمي لله ولا عدل له، كل خلقه يقر له ويعترف أنه خالقه، لا شريك له ولا مثل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r4.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r4.claim: Al-Raghib reads samiyyan as a counterpart who truly deserves God’s name and attributes, not merely someone sharing a name.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r4.anchor: وقال الراغب: وقوله تعالى: (هَلْ تَعْلَمُ لَهُ سَمِيًّا) أي نظيرًا له يستحق اسمه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r5.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r5.claim: Al-Raghib says divine names may be used of people, but their meanings differ when applied to God.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r5.anchor: إذ كان كثير من أسمائه تعالى قد يطلق على غيره، لكن ليس معناه إذا استعمل فيه سبحانه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r6.claim: The author suggests al-Raghib alludes to names such as ʿAli, ʿAziz, Raʾuf, and Karim, often used as shortened forms of names beginning with ʿAbd.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r6.anchor: قلت: لعله يسْير بذلك إلى مثل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r7.claim: The author notes that early Muslims also used honorifics such as al-ʿAli bi-Allah and al-Zahir bi-amr Allah.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r7.anchor: وجرى السلف على التلقب -: العلى بالله

NASHR:v1p284/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p284/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p284/r1.claim: In the large-idgham rule, the hāʾ's lengthened vowel has no independent status, so it is omitted in writing and does not block assimilation in لعبادته هل and similar cases.

NASHR:v1p284/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p284/r2.speaker: ابن مجاهد
NASHR:v1p284/r2.claim: Ibn Mujahid prefers leaving assimilation in this class: he says assimilation should remove only the first consonant's vowel, whereas these cases also remove the intervening wāw and the hāʾ's vowel.
NASHR:v1p284/r2.anchor: الداني عن ابن مجاهد أنه كان يختار ترك الإدغام

NASHR:v1p284/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p284/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p284/r3.claim: Ibn al-Jazari rejects Ibn Mujahid's restriction and says the correct practice is to assimilate the whole class without distinction, as the performance authorities agree.
NASHR:v1p284/r3.anchor: الصواب ما عليه إجماع أهل الأداء من إدغام الباب كله

NASHR:v1p284/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p284/r4.speaker: محمد بن شجاع البلخي
NASHR:v1p284/r4.claim: Muhammad ibn Shuja al-Balkhi explicitly transmits Abu Amr's assimilation in إلهه هواه; al-Abbas also reports it, and Abu Zayd transmits it in إنه هو التواب.
NASHR:v1p284/r4.anchor: روى محمد بن شجاع البلخي إدغامه نصا

NASHR:v1p284/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p284/r5.speaker: الكرزيني
NASHR:v1p284/r5.claim: Al-Karazini alone reports izhar at جاوزه هو, allegedly from Ibn Mujahid's students; Ibn al-Jazari instead endorses assimilating the entire class.
NASHR:v1p284/r5.anchor: انفرد الكارزيني بإظهار جاوزه هو دون سائر الباب.

NASHR:v1p284/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p284/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p284/r6.claim: The chapter lists eight yāʾ-followed-by-yāʾ sites for large assimilation, including يأتي يوم, ومن خزي يومئذ, والبغي يعظكم, ونودي يا موسى, and فهي يومئذ واهية.
NASHR:v1p284/r6.anchor: ثمانية مواضع يأتي يوم في البقرة

NASHR:v1p284/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p284/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p284/r9.claim: Ibn al-Jazari rejects the contrary reading attributed to Ibn Jubayr and Ibn Saʿdan from al-Yazidi as unsound.
NASHR:v1p284/r9.anchor: وما روي عن ابن جبير وابن سعدان عن اليزيدي من خلاف ذلك فلا يصح

NASHR:v2p11#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p11#2/r1.speaker: قالون
NASHR:v2p11#2/r1.claim: Qalun has both valid options: numerous authorities and al-Dani's reading from Abu al-Hasan give assimilation, while other authorities and al-Dani from Abu al-Fath give izhar; most assign them to Abu Nashit and al-Hulwani respectively, though al-Mubhegh reverses that assignment.
NASHR:v2p11#2/r1.anchor: والوجهان عن قالون صحيحان. وهما في التيسير

NASHR:v2p11#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p11#2/r2.speaker: خلاد
NASHR:v2p11#2/r2.claim: Most sources give Khallad izhar, but several transmit idgham from him; both readings are attested and sound by transmission and performance.
NASHR:v2p11#2/r2.anchor: والوجهان جميعا عن خلاد في الهداية والتيسير،

NASHR:v2p11#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p11#2/r3.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو جعفر وخلف وورش وخلف عن حمزة
NASHR:v2p11#2/r3.claim: These readers give izhar; some performance authorities also report it for Yaqub, but only outside the riwāyas of Rawh and Roways. Ibn al-Jazari says that is the established practice and his own reading.
NASHR:v2p11#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالإظهار وهم ابن عامر وأبو جعفر وخلف وورش وخلف عن حمزة

NASHR:v2p11#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p11#2/r4.speaker: صاحب المبهج وأبو العلاء
NASHR:v2p11#2/r4.claim: Al-Mubhegh uniquely gives Warsh via al-Asbahani idgham, and Abu al-Ala gives it via al-Hammami, contrary to the other transmitters from al-Asbahani.
NASHR:v2p11#2/r4.anchor: وانفرد صاحب المبهج بالإدغام عن ورش، يعني من طريق الأصبهاني

NASHR:v2p11#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p11#2/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو من رواية السوسي
NASHR:v2p11#2/r6.claim: Abu Amr through al-Susi assimilates a quiescent rāʾ into the following lām in examples including واصطبر لعبادته, يغفر لكم, and واصبر لحكم ربك.
NASHR:v2p11#2/r6.anchor: الراء الساكنة عند اللام نحو واصطبر لعبادته،

NASHR:v2p11#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p11#2/r7.speaker: الدوري
NASHR:v2p11#2/r7.claim: Reports differ from al-Duri: Ibn Shurayh, Abu al-Izz, and others transmit Abu Amr's idgham through this route.
NASHR:v2p11#2/r7.anchor: واختلف عنه من رواية الدوري. فرواه عنه بالإدغام أبو عبد الله بن شريح
